text_blocks.snippet: SIADH (Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone) can be a paraneoplastic syndrome, meaning it's associated with certain cancers. Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is the most common malignancy linked to SIADH, but it can also occur with other cancers including non-small cell lung cancer, mesothelioma, pancreatic cancer, and certain head and neck, brain, and GU (genitourinary) cancers. SIADH can also be caused by some chemotherapy drugs.
snippet_highlighted_words: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is the most common malignancy linked to SIADH, but it can also occur with other cancers including non-small cell lung cancer, mesothelioma, pancreatic cancer, and certain head and neck, brain, and GU (genitourinary) cancers

list.title: Paraneoplastic Syndrome:
list.snippet: In SIADH, the cancer cells, particularly in SCLC, can produce and release excessive amounts of antidiuretic hormone (ADH), also known as vasopressin. This leads to the body retaining too much water, causing low sodium levels in the blood (hyponatremia).
